validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM. The Alaska DNR Division of Oil & Gas 'Pipeline Services' record for this exact pipeline (dog.dnr.alaska.gov/Services/Pipeline/Nuiqsut%20Natural%20Gas) describes it by name, gives Status: Active, Diameters (in): 3.50, System Length: 14.40, Construction Dates: 01/01/1998-01/01/2001. The Nuiqsut Natural Gas Pipeline's 2013 Annual Comprehensive Report (filed with the state under ROW Lease ADL 416202, dog.dnr.alaska.gov/Documents/SPCS/Publications/LesseeAnnualReports/2013/2013AnnualReport-Nuiqsut.pdf) gives full engineering detail (route, pipe spec, pressure, capacity, construction and start-up history). The State of Alaska Online Public Notices lease-renewal package (aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/Attachment.aspx?id=120337, filed 2019-04-15) states 'NSB is 100% owner of the Nuiqsut Natural Gas Pipeline' and reviews ongoing O&M. This is a real, well-documented municipal pipeline, not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as 'transmission' - the 2013 Annual Report itself distinguishes the high-pressure 'Gas Transmission Pipeline' (1,440 psig, this GEM row) from the downstream low-pressure village 'Distribution System' (fed via a Pressure Reducing Valve station) - the two are NOT the same facility and GEM only tracks the transmission line, correctly. DUPLICATE: checked against all 41 other in-scope rows. The nearby North Slope entries (P7463 Northstar, P7465 Trans-Alaska/Kuparuk fuel-gas line, P6534 Point Thomson) and the Cook Inlet Kenai-Beluga family (P7450/53/54/55/56/58/61/64) are different facilities in different locations (Northstar Island, the TAPS pump-station fuel system, Point Thomson, and the Kenai Peninsula respectively) - none overlap the Alpine-to-Nuiqsut corridor. ROUTE CHECK: the routes-repo geometry (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7462.geojson, 1 feature, 35 points) runs from approximately 70.344N/150.928W (at the Alpine production pad complex) to approximately 70.218N/150.989W (at the village of Nuiqsut) - this matches the sheet's Alpine Development Project -> Nuiqsut termini and the sourced route description exactly; no route-vs-sheet mismatch. Only open items are the ATTRIBUTION concern on Operator (see fills[] and below) and two genuinely unsourceable MISSING_VALUE cells (Proposal, SegmentCost - see fills[], both UNRESOLVED).

validity.recommendation: Verify or correct Operator. Confirm whether an 'NSB Energy Management' department/division exists and operates this pipeline; if not, correct Operator to 'North Slope Borough'.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Operator reads 'North Slope Borough Energy Management'. Every primary document found (2013 Annual Comprehensive Report; the 2019 lease-renewal package) confirms North Slope Borough (NSB) - the municipal government itself - as lessee, 100% owner, and the entity responsible for the pipeline's operations. But neither document names an 'Energy Management' department: the 2013 Annual Report's own organizational table assigns day-to-day Operations & Maintenance responsibility to the 'Director of Public Works' (NSB Public Works department), with design/construction under NSB's CIPM department and overall authority in the Mayor's Office - no 'Energy Management' unit appears anywhere in either document. I could not independently verify 'Energy Management' as the operating division (web search was unavailable this session - search budget exhausted; NSB's current public department directory at north-slope.org also does not list an Energy Management department). This does not mean the value is wrong - NSB's internal org chart may have created an Energy Management division since 2019 - but it is unconfirmed by any source I could reach. Staged the conservative, well-documented value (the parent entity, North Slope Borough) as the fill and flagged the more specific claim here for a researcher with search access to verify.
